correctness.rationale: The exact coefficient-unitary matrix is factored into logarithmic dyadic diagonal slabs and a cross-slab rank-one Volterra matrix. Hardy factorable-matrix criterion gives bounded/compact thresholds. Exact finite-triangle singular values and bounded invertible local diagonal factors give nuclear slab mass (j+1)^(1-b) and explosive subunit quasi-Schatten slab mass. Summing a second dyadic decomposition of the cross-slab matrix proves it is trace class for b>1; trace-class pinching establishes necessity at b<=2 and yields finite-section nuclear growth with bounded additive error. Critical endpoint and all quantifiers rechecked. 482 supplementary finite numerical/algebraic checks passed, but infinite proofs do not depend on them.

value.rationale: The classical Dirichlet weight is the explicit critical exception to the known parameter-uniform Schatten range. A phase diagram with separate compactness, p>1, nuclear, and p<1 thresholds and logarithmic finite-section nuclear blowup answers a natural unresolved endpoint for a canonical logarithmically damped analytic-space operator. The order-of-growth results are useful to quantify finite-dimensional approximations, while exact constants remain open.
